[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty IAD55, matches an Inflect listing whose own building code exactly matches this rows name, giving 22515 Fitness Court, Sterling, VA.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's Northern Virginia (Ashburn/Loudoun/Sterling/Reston/Bristow/Fairfax) data center campus, one of the largest concentrations of colocation buildings in Data Center Alley. Digital Realty publishes individual building pages with real street addresses for most named buildings in this campus (for example IAD37 at 44060 Digital Loudoun Plaza Bldg K, IAD36 at 43780 Digital Loudoun Plaza Bldg H, IAD40 at 44372 Round Table Plaza Bldg M, VA4 at 8217 Linton Hall Road in Bristow, VA3 at 1780 Business Center Drive in Reston), confirmed via digitalrealty.com and third-party colocation marketplaces (UPSTACK, datacenterHawk).

reading.body:
Digital Realty's Northern Virginia campus, of which IAD55 is one building, operates as part of the largest concentration of colocation infrastructure in the United States, spanning multiple municipalities in Loudoun County and surrounding areas. The operator publishes approximately 600 MW of total IT load across this multi-building campus as of 2023, but does not publish a capacity figure specific to IAD55. The facility sits in Virginia, where 23 of 326 mapped data centers publish power figures, representing 1375.4 MW of disclosed capacity statewide.

IAD55 is a colocation building, which means it hosts multiple tenants rather than serving a single customer. The facility qualifies as part of infrastructure suitable for enterprise and cloud workloads typical of the Northern Virginia market, though the operator's published materials do not specify which tenants or workload types currently occupy this specific building. Its address at 22515 Fitness Court, Sterling, confirms it as a discrete structure within Digital Realty's larger regional footprint, rather than as a marketing designation for the campus as a whole.

The campus does not rank among Virginia's largest published data centers by disclosed capacity. Across the state's 23 facilities with published figures, this 600 MW campus ranks 24th, placing it outside the top tier of disclosed capacity. However, most mapped facilities in Virginia publish no power figure at all, meaning the true scale of unquantified capacity in the state is unknown. For investors or grid planners assessing Northern Virginia's role in AI infrastructure, the lack of building-specific published power figures limits visibility into whether this particular facility is growing to support accelerator workloads or remains oriented toward traditional colocation tenants.
